ABOUT THIS ATLAS

Know the data behind the map.

The atlas combines a historical public-sector facility inventory, the national strategic plan's care-level framework, a November 2025 neonatal resource assessment of 14 facilities, and dated public service and staffing records. Every record keeps its source and observation date.

Classification authority

General care levels follow the national strategic plan. Neonatal care levels are a clinical classification set by Dr Hammad Khan (dataset owner) on 5 November 2026, informed by the November 2025 workshop and mission reports; they are not inferred from equipment or facility type. Individual facility profiles refer back to this statement.

Public services & workforce

These records combine official inspections, audits, provider websites and clearly identified media accounts. Historic counts are headcounts, not current staffing or staff per shift. Cadre counts may overlap and are never summed. Staffing norms are reference requirements, separate from observed counts. Unknown fields remain unknown. Provider service listings do not verify operational readiness or individual equipment. Original neonatal assessment values remain separate.

Original sources

  • Facility Resource Assessment Report — extracted data, PATG workshop, 12–13 November 2025; prepared by Dr Hammad Khan and HF team. “Yes” for phototherapy means some equipment, insufficient capacity.
  • HF Paediatric medical mission report, 8–15 November 2025: tertiary neonatal care at EFSTH; mission paediatric surgery at EFSTH and Bansang. Surgery reflects mission activity only.
  • PATG Neonatal Capacity-Building Workshop report, 12–13 November 2025. Unattributed comments mention CPAP equipment, conflicting with the structured assessment’s all-“No” CPAP column; this map uses the structured table and retains that uncertainty.
  • Maina et al., 2019: public-sector health facility database (CC BY 4.0), accessed through an ArcGIS mirror: 101 Gambian facilities. This historical inventory is not a current operational register. Njau uses an explicitly approximate locality position.
  • Facility aliases reconciled against the strategic plan hospital names and NHIA hospital network. 2017 hospital renamings; Kanifing/Serekunda alias. Resource data attach to these matched facilities, not to neighbouring RCH centres.
  • National Health Sector Strategic Plan 2021–2025: this view uses the intended structure in section 4.1, printed pp.100–102: minor centres/community clinics → primary; major centres/district hospitals → secondary; general/teaching/specialised hospitals → tertiary. Six mapped hospitals are explicitly named in section 2.7.1 (p.22). Other tier assignments derive from historical facility types and require validation. Njau remains unclassified for general care.
  • Country outline: Natural Earth / geo-countries. Basemap: © OpenStreetMap contributors.

Two distinct care-level classifications

Neonatal services: November 2025 workshop context and the clinical classification described above: Bansang, Farafenni, Bwiam, Kanifing and Bundung MCH are secondary; EFSTH is tertiary (also documented in the mission report). These classifications are separate from the workshop equipment table. The neonatal view includes 14 retained assessment facilities: eight primary, five secondary and one tertiary. The eight previously unclassified assessment facilities were designated primary neonatal units in that classification. One facility from the source report has been excluded at the dataset owner’s request. Neonatal levels follow that clinical classification rather than being inferred from equipment or general facility type. The wider 102-facility dataset appears only in the general-services view.

General services: the strategic plan grouping described above. Generic clinic records are grouped provisionally from their historical source type, not from a current service audit. A general tertiary designation does not imply tertiary neonatal capability.

Strategic plan: source discrepancies

Section 2.7.2 (printed p.23) groups both major and minor health centres as secondary. The executive summary and section 4.1 instead place minor centres at primary level. The app consistently follows section 4.1’s intended structure and does not present it as a verified current operational classification. Section 2.7.1 also names Brikama, Soma, Essau and Basse as regional hospitals; this view retains the explicit section 4.1 major-centre/district grouping for these records, with that ambiguity stated in their profiles. The named Sheikh Zayed specialised hospital is absent from the historical map dataset, reinforcing that this is incomplete coverage.

Coverage & interpretation

Missing data means unknown, not absent. Coordinates marked approximate are locality-level placements, not confirmed facility entrances. This is a planning and exploration tool, not a live referral directory.
